name: Agency hero: the hero rewrites itself to answer whichever of four fears the visitor picks
notes: Signature effect: instead of arguing the case the author wants to make, the hero asks which case the visitor needs made. Four real fears as chips ('I paid someone and got nothing', 'I cannot afford to get this wrong', 'I do not have time for this', 'I do not know what I need'), and picking one rewrites the headline, body, evidence line and both calls to action together. The runner-up in the series recommendation, and the strongest converter of the ten on a cold visit. Built as a proper ARIA tablist with roving tabindex, arrow keys, Home and End, so a keyboard user tabs past the group in one press and navigates inside it with arrows. Heading semantics matter here and were fixed: an early version gave each of the four panels its own h1, putting four h1s in the markup. The hero's constant question is now the single h1 (carrying the service and market in a visually hidden span) and the four switching headlines are h2, which is what they actually are. Each part of a panel animates on its own small delay so the hero reads as re-set rather than swapped, and it is over in under half a second. Part of the ten hero 940Digital brand series (sections 0027 to 0036); the series log, the contact sheet that renders all ten live, and the written recommendation are in brand-heroes/set-evidence/. Unlike the client-derived sections in this library, this one is NOT de-identified: 940Digital is Owen's own business, so there is no third party to protect and the real wordmark, palette and copy are the point of the section. Brand rules baked in across the whole series: display type at weight 500 with about -0.03em tracking (not 700); #3194E0 never carries text on a light background because it measures 2.90:1, so blue text on sand is #1F6FB0 and a blue fill takes a charcoal label at 5.18:1; every figure is JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums; text containers are sized in ch, not px.
